title: Wendell and the Inheritance
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Wendell is found empty during a centennial exhumation, hotel concierge Ansel Underhill realizes the 'accidental' deaths of three people connected to Wendell's estate were murders tied to a decades-old land swindle. Working from guest ledgers, maintenance logs, and the habits of the powerful, Ansel maps who had access to the crypt and the case file. The killer turns out to be the town archivist, who has been quietly erasing records to protect the fortune's true heir—Wendell himself, who never died and has been living under a false name in Ansel's own hotel. In the climax, Ansel stages a fake statute-expiry deadline to force the archivist and the hidden Wendell into the open; Wendell dies confessing, and Ansel finally accepts being seen, taking a place on the town council.
about_author: Dominic Okonkwo spent eight years working night desks at grand hotels across three continents, collecting the small betrayals guests assume no one notices. He writes mysteries about invisible people who see too much.

chapters.title: The Empty Man
chapters.summary: Ansel Underhill narrates the centennial exhumation from the edge of the crowd, noticing which mourners flinch when the coffin opens on nothing. Police dismiss it as grave robbery, but Ansel recognizes the third 'accident' in two years among the pallbearers' names. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the uneasy thrill of finally being unable to look away.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ansel secretly cross-references hotel records with the leaked case file, discovering all three victims had handled documents about Wendell's original land grant—and that pages are missing from the town archive. Someone begins leaving warnings in Ansel's mailbox, quoting his own observations back at him. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: paranoia; invisibility curdling into vulnerability.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Checks Out
chapters.summary: Ansel identifies a long-term resident, 'Mr. Ellery,' whose routines match an aged Edmund Wendell, and realizes the archivist, Corinne Voss, has been both protecting and blackmailing him. When Ansel confronts Voss, she reveals the statute expires in nine days and offers him a bribe to stay invisible. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: temptation and fury—the corruption of power offered like a gift.

chapters.title: Centennial Night
chapters.summary: Ansel fakes the destruction of the surviving land-grant deed during the centennial gala, forcing Voss and Wendell to converge on the archive vault, where he has arranged for police and witnesses. Wendell collapses mid-confession; Voss is arrested with the missing file pages sewn into her coat. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: resolution—stepping out of the shadows, claimed at last by belonging.
